newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol, Moorfield in Teeside air cargo study.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol, Moorfield in Teeside air cargo study.

text.p: Amsterdam's Schiphol airport is involved in a feasibility study for a 250 acre airfreight terminal and industrial park at Teeside airport in north east England, a Schiphol spokeswoman said.

The go-ahead for the six-month study was signed earlier this week and other members include UK real estate company, Moorfield Estates Plc and Teeside local authorities, a Teeside airport spokesman added.

Complete development of the site could cost up to 340 million stg over several phases covering four to five years with eventual cargo capacity reaching one million tonnes annually against the existing figure of less than 800 tonnes, he said.

Under the plan, the airport would be able to handle up to six wide-bodied freighters bringing in parts for local assembly or onward distribution, meeting demand from the increasing of number of international firms installing themselves in north-east England, he added.

The proposal is backed by the Tees Valley Joint Strategy Committee which considers major planning matters on behalf of all five local authorities of Darlington, Hartlepool, Middlesborough, Stockton-on-Tees , Redcar and Cleveland, but the final planning decision will be taken by Stockton Borough Council, he said.

The Schiphol spokeswoman said it was the first time that the Dutch airport has taken an active role in the UK market, although it had been involved in initial discussions to see if there was potential for the project.
It is not yet clear whether the Dutch airport will take a financial stake in the project if it gets off the ground.

Schiphol is also involved in projects in New York, Vienna and Bogota on the international side. The Dutch airport has a one percent stake in Vienna airport. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
